name: St Mary's Church of England Infant School

areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for curriculum (12 specific items). Listed provision includes science are compulsory subjects, computing, teach computing, art, music.

signals.text: So, Relationships Education, Health Education and Science are compulsory subjects and parents/carers do NOT have the right to withdraw their children from these subjects.
signals.pageTitle: rshe a guide for parents and carers leaflet sep 2023 1

signals.text: Our curriculum is informed by a computing scheme, Teach Computing, that ensures progression of skills and covers all aspects of Computing in the National Curriculum.

The National Curriculum for Science (also a compulsory subject), includes learning the correct names for the main external body parts, learning about the human body as it grows from birth to old age and reproduction in some plants and animals (which could include human beings).
signals.pageTitle: rshe a guide for parents and carers leaflet sep 2023 1

signals.text: All classes will have scheduled Computing lessons either as a block topic, weekly lessons, or will be taught Computing alongside other curriculum subjects.
Implementation We follow a broad and balanced Computing curriculum that builds on previous learning and provides both support and challenge for all learners.

areas.narrativeSummary: The school website lists science are compulsory subjects, computing, teach computing, art, music. Information appears across 2 pages.

areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for enrichment and extra-curricular activity (11 specific items). Listed provision includes Improvise, art, delivery of art, art club, of an art club, music, computing.

signals.text: Music Knowledge and Skills Progression 2022 1: Improvise

In each lesson, children will participate in activities involving disciplinary and substantive concepts, developing their knowledge and understanding of Britain’s role in the past and that of the wider world.

Progress and the delivery of Art and design is monitored throughout the year with Sketchbook scrutinies, lesson visits and pupil and staff feedback The subject leader can then reﬂect on the quality of provision and review, troubleshoot and implement changes and provide support as necessary.
During the course of the year we supplement our programme of learning with the offer of an Art Club, often available for different year groups at different times of the year.
We actively encourage our more vulnerable children to access the extra-curricular opportunities on offer and are frequently reminded how music can develop a child’s development and confidence.

signals.text: It promotes the spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical development of pupils, preparing them for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences for later life.
We, like schools and parents, want children to be safe, healthy and happy.
signals.pageTitle: rshe a guide for parents and carers leaflet sep 2023 1

signals.text: Schools will be respectful of the faith, beliefs and contexts of children’s families, engaging with parents and carers.
signals.pageTitle: rshe a guide for parents and carers leaflet sep 2023 1

signals.text: Either way, it is important to remember these key points: • We all want children to be safe, healthy and happy.
